summary: The bad() entry point contains a CWE-510 trapdoor: it elevates a connecting client to admin ("Welcome, admin!") purely because the socket's reverse-DNS hostname resolves to "admin.google.com". Reverse DNS (getHostName()) is attacker-controllable, so this hardcoded hostname check is a hidden backdoor granting privileged access. The fix removes the hostname-based decision and instead gates the privileged greeting on an authentication token the client must supply, validated against a server-configured secret (read from the ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable). This preserves the two-outcome greeting feature (admin vs. user), keeps valid clients working, and does not return a constant result, while eliminating the spoofable-hostname trapdoor flow.
